1.0 Executive Summary & Problem Statement

In contemporary primary and secondary education, traditional examination systems suffer from a one-size-fits-all structural bottleneck. Every student receives the exact same set of questions regardless of whether they have already mastered the foundational concepts or are experiencing severe cognitive hurdles. Consequently, advanced students experience disengagement through boredom, while struggling students experience learned helplessness and heightened test anxiety.

Furthermore, although recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (LLMs) offer promising avenues for interactive learning, existing commercial implementations frequently suffer from:

  • Unbounded Latencies & Timeouts: Unary blocking HTTP requests that exceed 15 seconds during peak server demand, aborting connections abruptly.
  • Academic Dishonesty Risks: AI tutors that immediately reveal direct multiple-choice answer keys during live graded summative tests.
  • Hallucinated Telemetry: AI systems that fabricate student mastery metrics without grounding their reasoning in verified database records.
  • Digital Exclusivity: Modern cloud-heavy EdTech tools completely fail in rural schools lacking continuous internet connectivity.
AdaptIQ Solution: An enterprise-grade, psychometrically calibrated adaptive quiz and Socratic tutoring platform aligned with United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education). AdaptIQ unifies Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT), 1PL Rasch Item Difficulty Calibration, a multi-model Generative AI gateway with real-time Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming, and an authoritative dual-database layer (PostgreSQL + MongoDB).

3.0 System Architecture & Data-Flow Pipeline

AdaptIQ decouples client presentation, gateway routing, psychometric scoring, and AI generation into a robust, layered pipeline:

Core Architectural Pipeline:
React Frontend (SSE Reader) → AdaptIQ AI Gateway (Express) → Academic Integrity Guard (TestMode Lock) → Intent Classifier (Heuristic) → Model Router (AUTO/MANUAL) → Circuit Breaker / Fallback Cascade → Google Gemini 3.8 Flash / OpenAI / Anthropic / Ollama → Authoritative Dual DB (PostgreSQL + MongoDB)

Key Architectural Pillars:

  1. Confidential Server-Side Key Management: All AI provider API keys remain server-side in server/.env. The client bundle never exposes secrets.
  2. Granular Non-Blocking Lifecycle: Replaced monolithic 15s deadlines with 4 distinct limits: Connection (10s), First-Token (20s), Idle-Stream (20s), and Max Duration (120s), supplemented by 15-second heartbeat pings (: ping\n\n).
  3. Bidirectional Cancellation Propagation: When a student navigates away or clicks "Stop Generating", the frontend AbortController signals the server. The backend intercepts req.on('close'), halting the LLM stream to prevent wasted tokens.

4.0 Core Algorithms & Mathematical Formulations

AdaptIQ integrates 6 core mathematical algorithms grounded in cognitive science and psychometrics:

4.1 Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) Engine

Location: server/engine/bktEngine.js
BKT models a student's latent cognitive mastery of a specific skill as a hidden Markov state ($L_t \in \{0, 1\}$). Each time a student answers a question, the probability that they have mastered the concept ($P(L_t)$) updates based on Bayes' theorem:

If Correct: P(L_t | obs=1) = [ P(L_{t-1}) · (1 - P(S)) ] / [ P(L_{t-1}) · (1 - P(S)) + (1 - P(L_{t-1})) · P(G) ]
If Incorrect: P(L_t | obs=0) = [ P(L_{t-1}) · P(S) ] / [ P(L_{t-1}) · P(S) + (1 - P(L_{t-1})) · (1 - P(G)) ]
Skill Transition: P(L_{t+1}) = P(L_t | obs) + (1 - P(L_t | obs)) · P(T)

Default parameters: P(L_0) = 0.15 (prior), P(T) = 0.20 (learning rate), P(G) = 0.25 (guess rate), P(S) = 0.10 (slip rate). 

// server/engine/bktEngine.js
function updateMastery(pL_prev, isCorrect, params = {}) {
  const pL0 = params.pL0 ?? 0.15, pT = params.pT ?? 0.20, pG = params.pG ?? 0.25, pS = params.pS ?? 0.10;
  let prior = Math.min(Math.max(Number(pL_prev ?? pL0), 0.001), 0.999);

  let pL_obs;
  if (isCorrect) {
    pL_obs = (prior * (1 - pS)) / ((prior * (1 - pS)) + ((1 - prior) * pG));
  } else {
    pL_obs = (prior * pS) / ((prior * pS) + ((1 - prior) * (1 - pG)));
  }

  const pL_next = pL_obs + (1 - pL_obs) * pT;
  return Math.min(Math.max(pL_next, 0.001), 0.999);
}
Figure 4.1: Production implementation of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing updating $P(L_t \mid obs)$ and $P(L_{t+1})$.

4.2 1PL Rasch Item Difficulty Calibration Model (IRT)

Location: server/engine/raschEngine.js
In Item Response Theory, subjective teacher difficulty tags are replaced by empirical item difficulty ($b_i$) measured in Logits:

b_i = ln( f_i / p_i ) = ln( [1 - p_i] / p_i )

Where p_i = R_i / N_i (pass rate) and f_i = 1 - p_i (failure rate). Calibrates only when sample size N ≥ 30.

Figure 4.2: 1PL Rasch Log-odds Difficulty Calibration ($b_i$) with extreme-score continuity smoothing.

4.3 Leitner 5-Box Spaced Repetition Memory System

Location: server/engine/spacedRepetition.js
To counter the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve, reviewed concepts advance through 5 spaced intervals: Box 1 (1 day), Box 2 (3 days), Box 3 (7 days), Box 4 (14 days), Box 5 (30 days). Correct answers promote $+1$ box; errors demote immediately to Box 1.

Figure 4.3: Leitner 5-Box Spaced Repetition Memory Scheduling with Fibonacci day intervals.

4.4 Multi-Factor Unified Adaptive Difficulty Engine

Location: server/engine/adaptiveEngine.js
Real-time cognitive load balancing during practice:

  • Promotion: 3 consecutive correct answers escalates difficulty (EASY → MEDIUM → HARD).
  • Demotion: 2 consecutive incorrect answers de-escalates difficulty to prevent frustration and reinforce foundational concepts.
Figure 4.4: Multi-Factor Unified Adaptive Stepping Logic (3-streak promotion, 2-streak demotion).

4.5 Normalized Learning Gain (Hake's Average Gain $g$)

Location: server/utils/gradebookExporter.js
Measures student conceptual breakthrough independent of baseline pre-test score:

g = [ Post-Test Score - Pre-Test Score ] / [ 100 - Pre-Test Score ]

High Gain: g ≥ 0.70 | Medium Gain: 0.30 ≤ g < 0.70 | Low Gain: g < 0.30

Figure 4.5: Hake's Normalized Learning Gain ($g$) Engine with division-by-zero boundary protection.

4.6 Jaccard Text Similarity Question Deduplication

Location: server/services/gemini/responseValidator.js
Calculates token set overlap $J(A, B) = |A \cap B| / |A \cup B|$. AI questions with similarity $\ge 0.68$ to existing questions are automatically rejected.

5.0 Implementation Challenges & Engineering Resolutions

# Challenge Faced Root Cause Diagnosed Engineering Solution Implemented
1 timeout of 15000ms exceeded Client Axios instance had rigid timeout: 15000. Server geminiClient.js had hardcoded timeoutMs = 15000 in Promise.race. Complex generations took 16–22s, dropping connections. Raised client timeout to 60s. Implemented real-time Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming with granular server limits (10s connection, 20s token, 120s max). First token streams in < 1000ms.
2 Gemini 404 & Regional 503 Spikes Google deprecated gemini-2.5-flash for new accounts (404). Peak traffic triggered HTTP 503 UNAVAILABLE. Updated default model to gemini-3.8-flash. Built pre-stream fallback cascade that automatically tries gemini-3.8-flash → gemini-2.0-flash → gemini-1.5-flash → secondary providers.
3 Exam Integrity & AI Cheating Students could consult the AI Tutor during summative exams to obtain answers. Implemented Academic Integrity Lock: Backend checks for active post_test attempts created within 60 mins. If active, AI endpoints return 403 Forbidden with a policy guard notice.
4 Student PIN Brute-Force in Rural Schools Young students in grades 6–8 cannot remember 16-character passwords, requiring 4-digit PINs (vulnerable to brute-force). (1) 4-digit PINs scoped strictly within teacher's classroom joinCode; (2) 10-round salted bcrypt hash; (3) 5-req/min rate-limiting with 15-minute lockout after 5 failed attempts.
5 CSV DDE Formula Injection Student names or answers starting with =, +, -, @ could execute shell commands in Excel upon opening exported gradebooks. Implemented CSV sanitization: Every cell beginning with formula triggers is prepended with a single quote ('), and roll numbers are wrapped in ="007" formulas to preserve leading zeros.
6 Dual-Database Resilience Local PostgreSQL containers are not always running during offline testing, causing server startup crashes. Built safe Prisma proxy with 2000ms health check: If PostgreSQL is unreachable, server seamlessly falls back to MongoDB Atlas or ephemeral in-memory storage without dropping requests.

7.0 Deployment Architecture & Automated Testing

7.1 Deployment Models

  • Cloud Production (SaaS): React SPA hosted on Vercel/Netlify with global Edge CDN caching; Express API hosted on Render/Railway/AWS ECS behind NGINX with SSE proxy buffering disabled; managed Neon PostgreSQL + MongoDB Atlas clusters.
  • Rural Offline Classroom Gateway: Low-power single-board computer (Raspberry Pi 4/5 or local classroom mini-PC) running Docker Compose with PostgreSQL + Node backend bound to the classroom Wi-Fi LAN (LOCAL_LAN_BIND=0.0.0.0). Operates 100% offline with zero cloud dependency.

8.0 Conclusion & Future Scope

AdaptIQ proves that psychometrically grounded adaptive learning can coexist harmoniously with modern Generative AI. By deploying a centralized AI Gateway with Server-Sent Events, intelligent model routing, Socratic pedagogical modes, and robust circuit breakers, the platform delivers instant conceptual support while strictly protecting academic integrity and student privacy.

Future Enhancements:

  1. 2PL & 3PL IRT Calibration: Expanding the Rasch model with item discrimination ($a_i$) and pseudo-guessing ($c_i$) once response samples exceed $N \ge 1,000$.
  2. IMS QTI 3.0 Compliance: Modernizing assessment item packaging to QTI 3.0 JSON-LD standards.
  3. Multimodal Voice Tutoring: Real-time bidirectional voice interactions using the Gemini Live API for visually impaired students.
